text:
maya: Quick heads-up — customer 'FinReg-EU' on Private (VPC) flagged failed requests this morning. Control plane attempted fallback to a us-west model variant when eu-west capacity was tight and the packets were blocked by their egress rules.

carlos: ugh. Did the control plane treat Private the same as Hosted for fallbacks?

maya: looks like yes. Logs: `route_decision: fallback; target: model-7b-us-west; result: NETWORK_BLOCKED_EGRESS`. Attached error from agent: `connectivity error: tls handshake failed: remote unreachable`.

sree: That is expected from current policy — we prefer latency/cost tiers over region constraints unless customer has explicit allowed_regions set. For Private we thought egress restrictions would block cross-region fallback but apparently we just logged and moved on.

amelia: Important nuance: some Private installs are full-airgapped and will always block outbound. We must not try cross-region routing for those.

kevin: Agreed. Proposal: control plane rule: for Private deployments default to region-strict routing (no cross-region fallback). Add an opt-in flag `allow_cross_region_fallback: true` for customers who explicitly permit it.

maya: That makes sense. UX question: how do we expose that in Console? Customer confused when we silently routed and failed.

carlos: Console should show per-customer routing policy with a clear state: `region-strict`, `region-preferred`, `allow-cross-region`. And show last fallback attempt with outcome. Quick mock: `Routing policy: region-strict (blocked fallbacks: 1)`.

amelia: Also add telemetry: a metric `private_fallback_blocked_count` tagged by customer, region, model_variant. We need alerting for repeated blocked attempts (>=3 in 10m).

ops-bot: NOTE: Created incident INC-2026-042 on blocked fallback for FinReg-EU. Pager duty: on-call infra.

kevin: For API behavior, we should surface a response code when request fails due to disabled fallback vs network error. Right now it's just 5xx. Suggest new error `451` with message `region_fallback_blocked_by_policy` (451 used for unavailable for legal reasons but we can pick a new structured error).

maya: I'd prefer structured JSON error with fields `code`, `reason`, `route_attempts` so integrators can differentiate. Example: `{ "code": "RB-REGION-1", "reason": "fallback_blocked_by_private_policy", "attempts": ["eu-west (queued)", "us-west (blocked)"] }`.

sree: Implementation detail — runtime needs access to customer's allowed_regions mapping during routing. Today routing has only tier and cost hints. We'll surface a small read-only cache in the control plane with TTL 30s and immediate invalidation on policy change.

carlos: What about quotas? If we stop cross-region fallback, some customers will get throttled earlier. Need to reflect that in per-route quotas and in Console traffic projections.

amelia: Right — add a 'constrained_capacity' view to console that estimates effective throughput under region-strict routing. Also communicate to sales/SRE so they can offer Dedicated capacity if needed.

kevin: Rollout plan: 1) Opt-out safe switch — add `allow_cross_region_fallback` default false for Private. 2) Telemetry + alerting. 3) Console toggle + UX copy. 4) After 2 weeks, change default to region-strict at control plane. Canary: enable on 5 internal customers first.

maya: Can we add agent-side detection so we fail fast instead of trying to route? Agent already reports network policy via `egress_probe`. If `egress_probe` fails we short-circuit fallback decision.

sree: Good call. Add check: if `egress_probe` indicates blocked outbound for region X, mark customer as `egress_blocked` and don't attempt cross-region for duration TTL.

carlos: I’ll put up a short RFC + config snippet:

```
routing:
  default_policy: region_preferred
  private_default_policy: region_strict
  allow_cross_region_fallback: false  # per-customer override
  egress_probe_ttl_secs: 120
```

amelia: Can you also include console copy for the toggle? "Allow Redwood to route requests to a model instance outside your configured regions. Turning this on may cause traffic to leave your VPC if network rules permit."

kevin: Security acceptability: security team ok with opt-in only. Also require explicit consent recorded in audit logs. KMS/HSM unaffected.

ops-bot: ACTION created: ENG-PLAT-540 create policy flag + console toggle (assignee: carlos).

deploy-bot: scheduled deploy: routing-service v2.13.4 -> canary group tonight (02:00 UTC).

maya: Thanks — I’ll notify the FinReg-EU customer and escalate if they want cross-region fallback enabled. For now, let's make telemetry visible so support doesn't get blindsided. :+1:
